Ah yes, one of our many "windows to another world" skips. I'm honestly surprised by how under the radar this one is, so maybe some crosslinks will boost the attention. I feel an easy way to tie this one in to other skips would be to make a comparison between it, and a few other "WtAW" skips. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Change this:

SCP-675 is a standard window and frame found in the northwest portion of Observation Post 9010, in the living room area. During random time intervals, shadows resembling humanoid figures (designated as SCP-675-1) can be seen through the window. These shadows are visible at all times of the day and night, and are seen to be visually distinct from normal nighttime darkness. These instances are only visible from within Observation Post 9010.

To this:

SCP-675 is a standard window and frame found in the northwest portion of Observation Post 9010, in the living room area. During random time intervals, shadows resembling humanoid figures (designated as SCP-675-1) can be seen through the window. These shadows are visible at all times of the day and night, and are seen to be visually distinct from normal nighttime darkness. These instances are only visible from within Observation Post 9010. It is currently hypothesized that SCP-675-1 instances are trans-dimensional beings, and that SCP-675 functions similarly to SCP-1278 and SCP-1288 as a means of viewing them.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: REWRITE Overview
item.content:encoded:
Alright, the rewrite is now live. Thanks to CryogenChaos for helping me with the rewrite process, and to the various other people in chat who took a look at it and made suggestions.

I contacted the original author, Dr Talson, and got a lot of good feedback from him/her. I did my best to respect the author's opinions in this rewrite, and I made a lot of changes to the draft in order to reflect that.

The things that I tried to tackle in this rewrite:

1. Lack of interest in the actual effect

2. The fact that the shadow figures don't do anything

3. The lack of a solid twist

Comments and thoughts on the rewrite are welcome.

item.content:encoded:
The containment procedures mention that no one is allowed to tap on the window, and the [DATA EXPUNGED]s in the story of how the window came into the Foundation's possession imply something dramatic happening, but neither of those things are fleshed out, and the article is, as previous comments have agreed, severely underwhelming as a result. All two or three minutes I spent reading this article, I was waiting for at least one of those two points to be elaborated on, and I was very much let down when they weren't.

In short, the idea has some potential - even if it isn't terribly original - but the way it is, as far as I'm concerned, the article fails. Downvoted.
